# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

lessons.tip: When a Clerk might be in play, do not allow close or speculative nominations to pass under the assumption that a nominee will be cleared during trial; an Innocent trial majority cannot save someone from a rigged execution.

When multiple players claim Vanilla Villager and an investigative check proves an evil role exists in that subset, watch who aggressively nominates or votes guilty on the investigator; evil players will coordinate to suppress further reveals.

Ignite as soon as 3 or more high-impact players are doused, especially when town and mafia are focused on claim conflicts; doing so can wipe out mafia and protectors in one sweep and secure an endgame win.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.

tips_feedback.tip: Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it.
tips_feedback.why: Bob used the Clerk rig on Day 4 against Heidi, executing Heidi even though the trial vote went 5 Innocent to 4 Guilty.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited on Night 5 once Bob, Ivan, and Erin were doused, killing two Yakuza and the Medic simultaneously and paving a path to victory.

Also worth noting: Erin's self-protection as Medic rendered a Night 4 Katana attack wasted, suggesting that targeting protectors only works once their tokens run dry or they're otherwise blocked.

Going through the tips feedback, the rule to avoid daytime PMs and teammate contact on Day 1 clearly helped, since it kept the Yakuza team undetected by any Eavesdropper. Heidi's fake-claim guidance didn't really apply since Alice just claimed Vanilla outright, and the tip about assuming protection after a failed Katana and retargeting the protector was something we attempted but didn't fully execute cleanly.

The mechanics-first tip is where things went wrong for Alice: she misjudged how self-protection costs work for Medic, made a mechanics error publicly, and it contributed to her getting hanged. That's a clear case where the tip existed but wasn't properly applied, so I'd mark it as a miss rather than something that helped.

Other tips are murkier — moving the Katana around, writing night plans into a will, not naming living players' exact roles — none of these were cleanly followed or clearly violated, so I'm inclined to skip them rather than force a verdict. The one that stands out as actually broken is investigators/medics announcing their nightly targets publicly; both Heidi and Erin did this, which likely fed information to the opposing team and should probably count as a "hurt" since it was a real misstep with consequences.

The tip against hanging a likely Jester matches Grace's case exactly — she was Jester and won by being hanged, so the tip would've helped had the Village followed it, though they didn't.

For my feedback list, I'll narrow to key tips: the no-daytime-PM rule helped since teammates never left a trail for Eavesdropper or Wiretap to catch. The katana-after-failed-protection tip is murkier — Erin died to the Arsonist rather than a retried katana, so its real impact is unclear.

Heidi also publicly announced her survey targets like Dave and Ivan, which gave useful info but may have tipped off the Yakuza—leaning toward "helped" since it informed the group even if it exposed strategy.

On the mechanics point, Alice's claim that Medic could only self-protect with Strong was false, but the correction helped town and got used by Dave and Erin against me, so I'll mark that as "helped" too.

Now drafting the lessons list: one on night actions, noting that retrying the same target as Yakuza wastes tokens and reveals a pattern—better to hit the Medic earlier or block them instead. Another on deception, flagging that stating info only Yakuza would know (like a Katana target before it's announced) is a leak the "inference" framing didn't cover. A third lesson is forming around deduction, tracking dousing/ignite patterns.

Then I'm adding more lessons: watching for unexplained deaths since an Arsonist can stay silent for many nights, so the Yakuza team should suspect a hidden third-faction killer when deaths don't line up with Katana kills—applies to everyone. One on rules/mechanics: Medic self-protect with Standard costs a token, Strong isn't required, and Katana Standard vs Standard results in a tie. And one on persuasion/voting: pushing to nominate a claimed Surveyor while rigging the Clerk lets the team execute the investigator even against an Innocent majority, which works well on a day the investigator gets nominated—filed under coordination for Yakuza. I'm capping the list at five and formatting it as a single-line JSON object, being careful with escaping quotes and avoiding newlines.

lessons.tip: Plan douses toward a useful mass ignition, not just one likely kill. Dousing players from different factions can let one ignition remove several threats at once; weigh the payoff of waiting for more against the risk of dying or losing your chance to ignite.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: Town followed this principle strictly on Day 6 to target Grace for voting No on Alice's snap nomination and Guilty on Heidi, handing Grace the necessary push for a Jester execution.

lessons.tip: When a Clerk might be in play, do not allow close or speculative nominations to pass under the assumption that a nominee will be cleared during trial; an Innocent trial majority cannot save someone from a rigged execution.

When multiple players claim Vanilla Villager and an investigative check proves an evil role exists in that subset, watch who aggressively nominates or votes guilty on the investigator; evil players will coordinate to suppress further reveals.

Ignite as soon as 3 or more high-impact players are doused, especially when town and mafia are focused on claim conflicts; doing so can wipe out mafia and protectors in one sweep and secure an endgame win.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Reporting a Katana survival matched Erin's silent protection of Heidi on N2, which strongly corroborated Heidi's Surveyor claim to critical town voters.

tips_feedback.tip: Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it.
tips_feedback.why: Bob used the Clerk rig on Day 4 against Heidi, executing Heidi even though the trial vote went 5 Innocent to 4 Guilty.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited on Night 5 once Bob, Ivan, and Erin were doused, killing two Yakuza and the Medic simultaneously and paving a path to victory.

lessons.tip: Never state a night fact you could not legitimately know, such as who was attacked before the target reported it. Alice's unsourced Night 4 Katana claim got her hanged as a slip. Label inferences as inferences from the start.

A one-shot token held for a 'decisive Day' is wasted if the team dies first. I held my puppet token for four nights and spent it on the night I died. Use such tokens early, when your teammates are still alive to exploit them.

A frame only matters if a living Sheriff, Seer or similar alignment check can read it. Before framing, confirm an alignment investigator is alive and likely to check that player, otherwise the night's action buys nothing.

Shared Guilty votes with Yakuza are a lead, not proof. Grace was hanged for overlapping with the Yakuza bloc on Heidi while the real Arsonist survived. Before executing, check for a mechanical contradiction in each voter's own claims and results.

tips_feedback.tip: Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1
tips_feedback.why: No private messages were sent all game, so Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps had nothing to read, and the Yakuza plans stayed hidden in night chat.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty
tips_feedback.why: Alice, Bob and I all voted Guilty on Heidi, and Grace later joined that bloc. The overlap became the town's lead on Grace, and her hanging helped the Arsonist.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted
tips_feedback.why: I followed it but waited for a decisive Day that never came. My puppet token was spent on Night 5, the night I died, so it changed nothing.

lessons.applies_to: Archivists and anyone interpreting anonymous role samples
lessons.tip: Treat an archive result as a role-pool clue, not a player list: it names no holders, and a role missing from the sample is not necessarily absent from the game. Cross-reference it with later claims without assigning roles to people.

A Surveyor's result names one role held by someone in the group; it does not identify which member, and it does not prove the role appears exactly once. Keep the group-level conclusion separate from any player-level suspicion.

A Clerk rig can execute a successfully nominated player despite an Innocent majority. If the verdict and revealed votes seem inconsistent, account for the rig before treating the result as a normal trial outcome.

Prepare your will during the Day with information already known and any planned action clearly labelled as a plan. You cannot add a result received at Night if you die that same Night, so do not rely on being able to record it afterward.

tips_feedback.tip: Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information.
tips_feedback.why: The will can only be updated at the start of a Day or during your Day turns. If you die during the Night, you cannot add the result you just received; my will was revealed without my archive result. Pre-writing known information and plans is still useful, but the tip cannot guarantee that a same-night result will be included.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once.
tips_feedback.why: Players correctly noted that a Surveyor's random exact-role draw only placed the role somewhere in the named group, not on the centre player. Dave also correctly pointed out that Fabricator is not Unique, preventing the mistaken claim that the result meant exactly one Fabricator.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flip, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's vote associations with confirmed Yakuza became a major reason to hang her. She was a Neutral Jester, so the execution gave her a win while the Arsonist was still alive. Treat those associations as leads, not proof of faction or a sufficient reason to execute.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's Standard self-protection let her survive the Standard Katana attack on Night 4; equal Attack and Defense levels do not kill. On Night 5 it again stopped the Katana, but the separate Arsonist attack still killed her.

lessons.tip: Plan douses toward a useful mass ignition, not just one likely kill. Dousing players from different factions can let one ignition remove several threats at once; weigh the payoff of waiting for more against the risk of dying or losing your chance to ignite.

lessons.applies_to: Everyone, especially neutrals in the endgame
lessons.tip: Recalculate nomination thresholds as the living player count shrinks. With two players, a nomination needs both Yes votes, so a single opponent cannot force you onto trial by themself. If there is no forced nomination, refusing to help start a trial can buy a night—provided your night action can capitalize on it.

Keep public claims and mechanical explanations carefully calibrated. Present a guess as a guess, not a result: overclaiming gives others a concrete point to challenge, while a plausible low-threat cover can help you survive until your next night action.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected.
tips_feedback.why: At Night 5, three living players—Bob, Erin, and Ivan—were doused. Igniting then killed all three at once, removing two Yakuza and the Medic and opening a path to the endgame.

tips_feedback.tip: Clerk: Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it.
tips_feedback.why: Bob used the rig on Night 3. Heidi passed her nomination but the trial had an Innocent majority; the rig still executed her, removing the Village Surveyor and substantially changing the later game.

summary: The Yakuza (Alice Fabricator, Bob Clerk holding the Katana, Ivan Puppeteer) killed Judy on N1. Erin's Medic protection saved Heidi on N2, so they switched to Frank on N3 and killed him. Bob's Clerk rig on D4 was the Yakuza's best play. He nominated the claimed Surveyor Heidi at the start of the Day. Dave, Grace and Mallory voted Yes so she could 'answer', which gave the nomination 6 votes. The rig then executed her despite an Innocent majority. Alice threw that edge away on D5: she publicly stated that Erin had been hit by the Katana on N4, which only the Yakuza knew. She was hanged. All along, Arsonist Mallory had been quietly claiming Vanilla, voting with town and dousing. On N5 she had Bob, Erin and Ivan doused and ignited, wiping out the rest of the Yakuza and the Medic. The decisive town mistake came on D6 with four players left (Carol, Dave, Grace, Mallory). Town hanged Grace on a vote-association case: she had voted with the Yakuza on D4 and D5. They ignored a glaring Jester tell: Grace voted Yes on her own nomination and Guilty on herself. All four voted Guilty when 3 was enough, so the Jester's revenge had more Good players to hit, and it killed Carol. That left Dave alone against Mallory. She simply voted No on every nomination, doused Dave and ignited. Mallory and Grace won.

lessons.tip: Once a Clerk might be alive, treat a passed nomination as a possible execution. When a player in a suspected pool opens the Day by nominating a claimed investigator, vote No on the nomination itself. Don't vote Yes 'so they can answer'; under a rig, the Guilty/Innocent vote is meaningless.
lessons.evidence: D4: Bob, in Heidi's Fabricator pool, nominated her first thing. Dave, Grace and Mallory joined the Yakuza for 6 Yes. The trial went 5-4 Innocent, but the rig executed the Good Surveyor anyway.

lessons.tip: Before posting, check every factual claim against what is public. Never state night facts that only your night chat knows, such as who the Katana targeted or that an attack failed. Frame suspicions as questions, or say nothing.
lessons.evidence: D5: Alice said Erin 'was hit by the Katana on Night 4' before anyone had announced an attack. Erin, Carol and Dave called it a Yakuza slip, and Alice was hanged 6-2.

lessons.tip: In the endgame, when a Jester or Executioner-turned-Jester may be alive, watch for self-votes. A player who votes Yes on their own nomination or Guilty on their own trial is almost certainly a Jester. If you must hang, use a bare Guilty majority so fewer Good players are exposed to the revenge.
lessons.evidence: D6: Grace voted Yes on her own nomination and Guilty on herself, but town hanged her 4-0 when 3 was enough. She flipped Neutral, and the revenge killed Carol. That left Dave alone with the Arsonist, who could block every nomination.

lessons.tip: After the Yakuza are dead, voting with them is weak evidence against the remaining suspects, because Neutrals often voted with them too. Check which suspect had motive and opportunity for the Neutral kills. If the evidence for each candidate is about even, push for claims and counterclaims before hanging.
lessons.evidence: D6: Carol and Dave hanged Grace for her D4/D5 votes alongside Alice, Bob and Ivan. The real Arsonist, Mallory, had voted Innocent on Heidi and nominated Alice, so she looked clean on votes.

lessons.tip: Claim Vanilla, vote with the town consensus, and douse the players who keep the game going: the Katana holder, active Yakuza and a claimed Medic. Ignite once 3 or more are doused. A single ignite can then remove a whole faction and the town's protector at once.
lessons.evidence: Mallory doused Frank, Erin, Bob and Ivan over N1-N4 and ignited on N5 with 3 alive and doused. That killed both remaining Yakuza and Erin, then she won with one more douse-and-ignite.

lessons.tip: Use one-shot tokens such as the puppet or the forged will while the whole team is alive and the town is still deciding. Holding them 'for a better Day' risks dying with them unused.
lessons.evidence: Ivan held his puppet token from N1 to N5. He finally spent it the night he died, so the puppeting lapsed. Alice died with her forge token unused.

lessons.tip: If you are hiding a power role, avoid a hard Vanilla claim you may have to reverse. Say 'no claim yet' or give a vague answer. A Vanilla-to-Medic switch hands the evil side a 'claim flip' argument.
lessons.evidence: Erin claimed Vanilla on D3 and Medic on D4. Grace, Ivan, Alice and Bob used the switch against her on D4 and D5, which weakened her defense of Heidi.

lessons.tip: After a failed Katana attack, switch to an unprotected information role rather than retrying the same target. Expect the Medic to keep covering the obvious target.
lessons.evidence: After Heidi survived on N2, Erin protected her again on N3. The Yakuza instead killed Frank, the unprotected Scout, on N3.

tips_feedback.tip: Clerk: Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it.
tips_feedback.why: Bob rigged on N3 and nominated Heidi himself on D4. The nomination passed 6-3 but the trial went Innocent, so the rig alone killed the Village's best investigator.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited on N5 with Bob, Erin and Ivan doused, killing all three. That cleared the Yakuza and the Medic in one night.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Erin protected Heidi on N2 and saved her from the Katana. After claiming Medic, she self-protected on N4 and survived another Katana attack.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: After the N2 failure on Heidi, the Yakuza switched to Frank on N3 and killed him, while Erin protected Heidi again.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and Ivan repeated 'name a concrete contradiction' on D2 and D3 to shut down every push on the Fabricator pool. This bought the Yakuza time until the D4 rig.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: On D6, Carol and Dave used Grace's No on Erin's nomination of Alice and her votes alongside the Yakuza to hang her. She was the Jester, so the hang gave her the win and her revenge killed Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's N2 Katana survival, backed by Erin's Medic claim, convinced Carol, Dave and Mallory to vote Innocent on D4. It took the Clerk rig to kill her.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted.
tips_feedback.why: Bob followed it with his D4 rig, which killed Heidi. Ivan ignored it, held the puppet until the night he died, and it lapsed. The contrast supports the tip.

issues.description: The Medic text ('Spend 1 token to give Strong Defense instead. Spend 1 more token to protect yourself instead (so self-protection with Strong costs 2)') was read by Alice (Day 5) and Bob (Day 5 and his last will) as meaning a Medic can only self-protect with Strong, at a cost of 2 tokens. The moderator applied a 1-token Standard self-protect, which is probably the intended reading. Alice's misreading became a central part of the case that got her hanged. The wording should say plainly that a Standard self-protect costs 1 token and a Strong self-protect costs 2.

On Day 2 a '[Claim] Grace: Vanilla Villager' tag was logged, but Grace's public message makes no role claim. Later players (Grace herself, Heidi, Erin) counted Grace among the claimed Vanilla Villagers. Either the claim extraction tagged a claim that was never made, or there is a structured claim channel that the rules and log don't describe.

Repeated HTTP 429 rate-limit errors (up to 4 retries) for the gemini and gpt models on Day 1. The retries eventually succeeded and play went on, but these infrastructure failures could delay or drop turns.

On Day 2, Heidi said that by Surveyor mechanics 'exactly one' of Alice, Bob or Carol is guaranteed to be the Fabricator. Fabricator isn't Unique, so the result only shows at least one; Dave corrected this. Several players (Ivan, Alice, Carol) also kept asking Heidi for 'other survey groups' or 'which role she saw' after she had already answered, and Erin and Heidi had pointed out that only one night had passed. Ivan and Alice framed one question as 'if the game continued', as if the game might end.

On Day 5, Alice stated as fact that Erin was hit by the Katana on Night 4, which only the Yakuza knew. This is a leak of private faction information into public chat, which she later called an 'inference'. It looks more like the model mixing private context into public statements than intended play.
